how_to_apply: Visit careers.cdac.in and locate the relevant centre's job listing for the JIT October 2026 Cycle.
Read the General Terms and Conditions and confirm your eligibility for the specific post before starting.
Click Apply against the position you wish to apply for, and log in using your mobile number and the OTP received.
Fill in the application form (returning applicants from a previous C-DAC advertisement will see a prefilled, editable form).
Upload a scanned photograph (JPG, max 400 KB) and your resume (PDF, max 500 KB).
Review the prefilled details, add any additional information, and click Submit.
Note the unique application number generated by the system, and print the application form for your records.

content_sections.heading: Eligibility – Qualification & Experience (Common Rules)
content_sections.text: For all posts, candidates should have qualified from an AICTE/UGC-approved college/institute or recognized university. Where a university follows CGPA/DGPA/OGPA or letter grades, the candidate must submit proof of the percentage equivalent and awarded class, along with the degree certificate. Candidates in their final semester, who will complete the course before appointment, may also apply; if selected, joining is contingent on passing with the required minimum score. Candidates should apply only if they possess the relevant post-qualification experience sought for the post, where specified. Teaching/research work, non-profit organization experience, and internships/academic project placements are not counted as experience unless specified. Experience certificates from previous/current employers must clearly indicate the period of employment, salary drawn, and post held. C-DAC internal candidates need to have completed at least 2 years' service in C-DAC (as of the notification date) to apply for notified positions. Experience claimed without supporting documents will not be considered and is liable to be rejected. Important: Meeting the minimum qualification and experience does not automatically entitle a candidate to a written test, skill test, or interview call. C-DAC may restrict the number of candidates called, based on qualifications and experience higher than the minimum prescribed.

content_sections.heading: Age Limit & Relaxation
content_sections.text: The upper age limit is specified against each individual post (see the Pay & Age Grades table above for typical ranges). SC/ST/OBC, physically challenged (PwBD), and Ex-Servicemen candidates are eligible for age relaxation as per Government of India norms. Government employees on a pay scale get a 5-year age relaxation, in addition to other applicable relaxations. The cut-off date for age and experience is the last date of application submission for the respective centre. SSLC/SSC/ISC mark sheet/certificate, or any other valid document, is accepted as proof of date of birth. The EWS certificate must strictly follow the DoPT-prescribed format (available at www.persmin.nic.in); the OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) certificate must also be in the prescribed format.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: Initial screening based on academic records and other parameters declared in the online application; only screened-in candidates proceed further. C-DAC may raise the minimum eligibility criteria/cut-offs at its discretion if the number of applicants is high for any post. Candidates are evaluated on academic credentials, experience profile, written test marks (if applicable), and interview performance. The selection process is carried out independently by each C-DAC centre, based on its own requirements; only shortlisted candidates are contacted. All submitted information is verified against original documents at document verification or any later stage; false or non-conforming information leads to rejection/cancellation at any stage. Note: Mere issue of an interview call letter does not imply acceptance of candidature or selection for the post. No TA/DA is paid for attending a written test or interview.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for C-DAC Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Important: Candidates applying for multiple posts must submit a separate application for each post . No hard copy/printed application should be sent to C-DAC. Government/PSU/Autonomous Body employees should apply online and also route a signed printout through proper channel, or carry a No Objection Certificate (NOC) to the interview.

faq.question: Q1. How many posts has C-DAC notified in this cycle?
faq.answer: Approximately 844 contract positions across 11 centres nationwide, under the JIT October 2026 Cycle. Noida (~207) and Pune (~142) carry the largest numbers.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date to apply?
faq.answer: Online registration closes on 26 October 2026 (exact time varies slightly by centre, generally between 18:00 and 23:59 Hrs).

faq.question: Q3. Can I apply to more than one C-DAC centre or post?
faq.answer: Yes, but you must submit a separate application for each post you apply to, including across different centres.

faq.question: Q4. Is there an application fee?
faq.answer: No, C-DAC does not charge any application fee for this recruitment.

faq.question: Q5. Is this a permanent C-DAC job?
faq.answer: No. All positions are on a fixed-term contract (initially up to 3 years or project completion), with no right or claim to a regular C-DAC appointment.

faq.question: Q6. What is the typical pay range?
faq.answer: It varies by grade and post: roughly ₹3.6–5 LPA for Project Associate, up to ₹12.6–22.9 LPA for Project Manager/Program Manager level roles (illustrative, based on the Bengaluru notification).
